articleSummary: Chandipura virus outbreaks in Gujarat have caused 22 child fatalities during the current monsoon season, with 35 positives among 184 tested cases, prompting intensified surveillance and testing by the Gujarat Health Department. First identified in 1965 in Chandipura, Maharashtra, CHPV is mainly reported in central and western India, including Gujarat, Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh. It is vector-borne, primarily by phlebotomine sandflies; mosquitoes and ticks may contribute. Transmission peaks in monsoon/post-monsoon due to humid conditions. Symptoms start with fever, severe headache, vomiting, and fatigue, progressing to seizures, confusion, drowsiness, brain swelling, or coma. No vaccine or specific antiviral exists; diagnosis uses RT-PCR or IgM ELISA. Prevention focuses on sandfly bite avoidance and environmental management. Early hospitalisation is crucial to reduce fatalities.

articleSummary: TBScreen.AI, an AI-based chest X-ray scanner developed by Universitas Gadjah Mada (UGM), accurately detects tuberculosis (TB) and has undergone external validation across five Indonesian health facilities as of 5 August 2026. articleSummary: Chikungunya vaccine platform uses a genetically modified Chikungunya virus that can replicate once but cannot mature into an infectious form, providing protection without disease. By replacing the furin-cleavage region with a sequence from tobacco mosaic virus and using human LoVo cells lacking furin, the virus is 'activated' for a first replication but then remains immature and non-infectious, serving only as antigen. articleSummary: Mpox (monkeypox) samples were smuggled into the United States by NIH virologists Vincent Munster and Claude Kwe, who were stopped Jan 25 at Detroit Metropolitan Airport after returning from the Republic of the Congo and Paris; they were arrested June 2 on charges of conspiracy to smuggle mpox and lying to border agents. The samples were inactivated, confirmed by FBI testing, and were allegedly intended for diagnostic development to track viral evolution, test sensitivity to new variants, and evaluate vaccines and treatments. The defendants face up to five years in prison; they have been suspended and barred from the Rocky Mountain Laboratories campus in Montana. The case underscores regulatory compliance: import permits, inactivation certification, select agent rules, and biosafety reviews. Scientists warn the episode highlights paperwork risk rather than public danger and may deter participation, potentially slowing outbreak detection and pandemic preparedness, amid funding gaps for mpox and Ebola responses.
notes: サンプルは不活化されており、FBIの検査でも確認済み。記事は研究規制・バイオセーフティ法令遵守および資金不足によるアウトブレイク対応能力低下への懸念を扱ったものであり、DRCやその他対象国での実際の感染症発生を報告するものではない。

articleSummary: Influenza (flu) remains active into summer in Greece, with rising cases among teenagers and young adults on holiday. Health centers on popular islands have prescribed hundreds of antivirals recently. Transmission is linked to crowding in beach bars, clubs, ships, and narrow streets, reflecting travel-driven mixing. Southern Hemisphere data show Australia and New Zealand with the strongest activity, with Brazil and Chile also increasing and co-circulation of influenza A and B. Travelers from these regions could import the virus to the Northern Hemisphere. Epidemiologists monitor the South to guide surveillance and the selection of strains for Europe’s next winter vaccines. In Greece, community positivity was under 10% by early July; there have been sporadic new admissions but no ICU cases. Symptoms range from mild to severe: fever, chest pain, cough (productive or dry), runny nose, myalgias, sore throat, hoarseness. Seek care if fever persists or breathing difficulty occurs.

articleSummary: On 6 August 2026, the Democratic Republic of Congo reports Ebola deaths exceeding 1,800 and 3,973 confirmed cases, with a sharp ongoing rise: two weeks earlier under 1,000 deaths and under 2,500 cases. The current outbreak is driven by the rare Bundibugyo ebolavirus variant, for which, unlike the more common Zaïre (Zaire) strain, there is no vaccine or treatment available for it. Public health authorities are monitoring the escalation and the lack of available therapeutics.

articleHeadline: 印度22名儿童感染金迪普拉病毒死亡|光华网
articleSummary: Jindipula virus outbreak in Gujarat, western India, with 184 suspected cases and 35 laboratory-confirmed infections as of August 3; 22 deaths and 7 critical among patients all under 15 years old. India’s Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has deployed a National Joint Epidemic Response Team to Gujarat for epidemiologic assessment, investigation, and clinical management. The National Centre for Disease Control notes that Jindipula virus, a member of the Rhabdoviridae family, periodically causes outbreaks in western and central India, especially during the monsoon. Transmission is via sandfly bites. Symptoms include high fever, severe headache, nausea, and fatigue; severe cases can spread to the brain, causing vomiting, seizures, and loss of consciousness. Without timely treatment, illness can progress to coma or death within 48–72 hours. There is currently no approved antiviral drug or vaccine for Jindipula virus.
notes: ジンディプラウイルスはRhabdoviridae科に属し、サシチョウバエ媒介で西・中央インドでモンスーン期に周期的に発生。ワクチン・抗ウイルス薬は未承認で、致死率が高く小児に重篤な影響を及ぼしている。
